::: {.lead}
Today you review Lectures 1–14 with two experiments on the lab computer:
a notice made with AI help in Word, and a price list in Excel. There are no
new ideas: you use what the lectures taught. **Part A** is in the apps;
**Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive page: on paper, scan its QR
code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in
its box.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word, Excel, a browser and an AI
  assistant that the university allows (for example
  `copilot.microsoft.com`).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Office.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive page, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

## Experiment 1 · A notice with AI, in Word

**The idea (Lectures 1–10):** a clear prompt has a task, a context and a
format. You check every fact of an AI answer and delete what you did not
give. Keep Text Only pastes plain text into Word; the style Title makes the
first line a title. A good file name starts with the date, and a PDF copy
keeps the look.

**Aim:** make a short notice with AI help, check it, and save it twice.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (an AI assistant and Word)**
:::

1. The library of the college closes early on **Sunday at 2 pm** because of
   a meeting. Ask an AI tool: *Write a notice of 3 short sentences for
   students: the library closes at 2 pm on Sunday because of a meeting.*
   Check every fact, and delete every fact that you did not give.

   {{< record "A fact that I deleted (or: none)" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good notice: "Library notice. The library closes at 2 pm on Sunday
   because of a meeting. Thank you for your understanding." Delete any
   added fact, for example free books or another day.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI adds "Books are free this week." Nobody said it. What do you do?

   - [x] Delete it.

     Why: Only the facts that you gave stay in the notice.

   - [ ] Keep it: it sounds nice.

     Why: An invented fact is wrong, even when it sounds nice.

   - [ ] Send the notice at once.

     Why: You check every AI answer before you use it.
   :::

2. Paste the text into Word with **Keep Text Only**. Give the first line
   the style **Title**, and make *2 pm* **bold**. Save it in Documents as
   `2026-11-29_library-notice.docx` (use today's date), and save a **PDF**
   copy too.

   {{< record "My two files: …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Two files with the same name: **2026-11-29_library-notice.docx** and
   **2026-11-29_library-notice.pdf**. The first line has the style Title,
   and 2 pm is bold.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Nobody may change the notice that you send. Which file do you send?

   - [x] the .pdf file

     Why: A PDF keeps the look, and people do not easily change it.

   - [ ] the .docx file

     Why: Anybody with Word can change a .docx file.

   - [ ] a photo of the screen

     Why: A PDF is clearer, and it keeps the text.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-08/sims/huda-day.html" poster="../../week-08/sims/huda-day.png" title="Huda's Busy Day: one job every hour" kind="game" >}}

3. Play **Huda's Busy Day** from 8:00 to 11:00: a file name, a share link,
   a prompt and its check. How does Huda share the price list with Rana at
   9:00?

   {{< record "At 9:00, Huda shares it with …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **A share link from the cloud, only for Rana, Can edit**: only the
   person who needs the file gets it, and she must change it.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which file name does Huda choose at 8:00 for the price list of 3
   November 2026?

   - [x] 2026-11-03_price-list.xlsx

     Why: The date first (year-month-day), what it is, no spaces.

   - [ ] new list final.xlsx

     Why: Spaces, "final" and no date.

   - [ ] Book1.xlsx

     Why: It does not say what the file is.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Prices with tax in Excel

**The idea (Lectures 11–14):** a formula starts with =, and **\$F\$1** stays
the same when you copy it. SUM adds a range. Sort puts whole rows in order;
a colour rule follows the numbers; a chart needs a real title.

**Aim:** build a price list with tax, and answer questions about it.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Excel)**
:::

1. Rana sells five items: Notebook 2 JD, Pen 0.5 JD, Bag 12 JD, Folder
   1.5 JD and Bottle 4 JD. Type *Item* and *Price (JD)* in A1 and B1, the
   five items under them, and **10%** in F1. In C2 write the tax
   **=B2\*\$F\$1**, and in D2 the price with tax **=B2+C2**. Copy both down
   to row 6. In D8 write **=SUM(D2:D6)**.

   {{< record "D4 (the bag) … ; D8 …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The bag: **13.2 JD** (12 + 1.2). D8 shows **22** (the five prices with
   tax: 2.2 + 0.55 + 13.2 + 1.65 + 4.4).
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="22" unit="JD" hint="The prices add up to 20 JD; the tax adds 10 %."}
   What does D8 show with `=SUM(D2:D6)`?

   Why: The prices add up to 20 JD, and 10 % tax adds 2: 22 JD.
   :::

2. Sort the table by the price with tax, largest first. Make every price
   with tax **above 4 JD** green with a rule (Greater Than 4). Then make a
   column chart of the prices with tax, with a real title, and save the
   file as `prices.xlsx`.

   {{< record "On top … ; green cells … ; my title …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   After the sort the **bag (13.2)** is on top. The rule colours **two**
   cells green: 13.2 and 4.4. A real title, for example "Prices with tax
   (JD)".
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   After the sort, largest first, which item is on top?

   - [x] the bag, 13.2 JD

     Why: The biggest price with tax comes first, with its whole row.

   - [ ] the notebook, the first item that you typed

     Why: Sort changes the order of the rows.

   - [ ] the pen, 0.55 JD

     Why: The smallest price goes to the bottom.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-06/sims/reference-lab.html" poster="../../week-06/sims/reference-lab.png" title="Reference Lab: copy a formula with $" >}}

3. In **Reference Lab**, copy =B2\*F1 down, see what goes wrong, then fix
   it with \$F\$1. What is the formula in C5 after the fix?

   {{< record "C5 after the fix: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **=B5\*\$F\$1**: B moved with the row, and \$F\$1 stayed. Without the \$,
   F1 moved to empty cells and the discounts became 0.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You copy `=B2*$F$1` from C2 to C3. Which formula is in C3?

   - [x] `=B3*$F$1`

     Why: B2 moves with the row; $F$1 stays.

   - [ ] `=B3*$F$2`

     Why: The $ signs keep F1: it does not move.

   - [ ] `=B2*$F$1`

     Why: B2 has no $, so it moves to B3.
   :::
